# Module `lune_ui_core::widgets::tree_view`

[API reference](../../INDEX.md) / parent [`lune_ui_core::widgets`](../widgets.md)

The tree view (`layout.tree-view`, D151): the app's pre-order rows with depths, a keyboard
cursor, single selection, guide lines, a disclosure mark and one block of rows in expand
motion, on a
[`scroll area`](scroll_area.md) that knows the whole extent.

State is sets of keys ([`TreeState`](tree_view.md#struct.TreeState), persistent), so expansion and selection outlive a rebuilt
row list and rows that scroll away. Each frame one walk over the rows gives the visible ones;
everything after it is index arithmetic, and only the rows in view are built. Rows are placed
with an `f64` subtraction and a cast of the small result, as in the virtual list, which is why
the tree sits on [`Ui::scroll_area_untranslated`](../ui.md#method.Ui.scroll_area_untranslated).

Frame order: the walk reads what changed in `expanded` since the last frame, whoever changed it
(a press, an accessibility action, the app), and fixes the cursor; the keys run, each toggle
walking again; the area and the rows follow. A press changes `expanded` after the walk, so its
block moves from the next frame; a key's moves in the same frame.

Expand motion: one key changed between two walks starts the block of its children, a change of
the moving key retargets it from where it is, and any other change snaps it. The rows of the
block keep their height: they draw under a clip of the block's current height, with no hit
regions and no nodes, and `cells` is not called for them, since it could add both. The rows
below sit at a closed-form distance, and the extent follows. When the block settles it stops
existing, so the frame after is the frame of the same state with no motion. Under a tier with
no expand motion it never exists.

The disclosure mark (a solid triangle, or a thin chevron: [`ChevronStyle`](tree_view.md#enum.ChevronStyle)) is drawn by the
tree, not as a glyph, and turns about its centre from 0 deg (closed, pointing right) to 90 deg
(open, pointing down). Its angle is the block's own fraction, so it lands with the rows and
needs no second animation: with no block (Reduced, Off, an app change of several rows) it is
exactly 0 or 90 deg and nothing is rotated. A press changes `expanded` after the walk, so the
mark turns from the next frame with the block. The guides ([`GuideStyle`](tree_view.md#enum.GuideStyle)) are quiet
(`Theme::tree_guide`); `OnHover` fades them in while the pointer is over the tree.

Source: `crates/lune-ui-core/src/widgets/tree_view.rs:1`

<a id="enum.GuideStub"></a>
### Enum `GuideStub`

```rust
pub enum GuideStub {
    Label,
    Short,
}
```

How far an elbow's stub reaches into a row with no mark of its own, in a tree that keeps a
mark slot on every row. A row with a mark always stops its stub before the mark's slot.

Source: `crates/lune-ui-core/src/widgets/tree_view.rs:128`

**Variants**

- <a id="variant.GuideStub.Label"></a>`Label`

  Across the empty mark slot, to [`LABEL_GAP`](tree_view.md#constant.LABEL_GAP) before the glyph or text, so the line
  points at the label.

- <a id="variant.GuideStub.Short"></a>`Short`

  To [`STUB_GAP`](tree_view.md#constant.STUB_GAP) before the mark slot, as on a row with a mark; the empty slot stays bare.

```rust
pub enum GuideStyle {
    Elbow,
    Straight,
    OnHover,
}
```

How the guide lines of the rows are drawn.

Source: `crates/lune-ui-core/src/widgets/tree_view.rs:115`

**Variants**

- <a id="variant.GuideStyle.Elbow"></a>`Elbow`

  A trunk through each ancestor's column and a rounded elbow into the row.

- <a id="variant.GuideStyle.Straight"></a>`Straight`

  One faint vertical line per depth, whether or not the ancestor is the last child.

- <a id="variant.GuideStyle.OnHover"></a>`OnHover`

  The elbow lines, at an opacity that fades in while the pointer is over the tree.

## Functions

<a id="fn.column"></a>
### Function `column`

```rust
pub fn column(k: u16) -> f32
```

The x of guide column `k`, from the row's left edge: the centre of the mark slot at depth `k`,
snapped to a pixel's centre so the 1 px line is crisp. The mark of a row at depth `k` is
centred here too, so the line meets its tip.

Source: `crates/lune-ui-core/src/widgets/tree_view.rs:290`

<a id="fn.guide_paths"></a>
### Function `guide_paths`

```rust
pub fn guide_paths(
    depth: u16,
    last: bool,
    ancestors: &[u16],
    height: f32,
    stub: f32,
) -> Vec<Vec<[f32; 2]>>
```

The lines of one row's guide, each a polyline in px from the row's top-left corner: a full
height line per column in `ancestors` (column `k` is the line of the rows at depth `k + 1`),
then the row's own. Not last: a trunk through the row and a branch off it. Last: one line that
turns into the stub. A row at depth 0 has no guide of its own.

Source: `crates/lune-ui-core/src/widgets/tree_view.rs:236`

<a id="fn.straight_paths"></a>
### Function `straight_paths`

```rust
pub fn straight_paths(depth: u16, height: f32) -> Vec<Vec<[f32; 2]>>
```

The lines of one row's guide in [`GuideStyle::Straight`](tree_view.md#variant.GuideStyle.Straight): a full height vertical line in the
column of every depth above the row's own (column `k` is the line of the rows at depth
`k + 1`, as in [`guide_paths`](tree_view.md#fn.guide_paths)). A row at depth 0 has none.

Source: `crates/lune-ui-core/src/widgets/tree_view.rs:269`

<a id="fn.stub_end"></a>
### Function `stub_end`

```rust
pub fn stub_end(depth: u16, bare: bool, stub: GuideStub) -> f32
```

Where the elbow's stub of a row at `depth` ends, from the row's left edge. `bare` is a row
with no mark in a tree that keeps a mark slot: [`GuideStub::Label`](tree_view.md#variant.GuideStub.Label) carries its stub across
the empty slot to [`LABEL_GAP`](tree_view.md#constant.LABEL_GAP) before the label; otherwise it ends [`STUB_GAP`](tree_view.md#constant.STUB_GAP) before the
row's content.

Source: `crates/lune-ui-core/src/widgets/tree_view.rs:279`
